findings.source_locator: interpolation.tex lines 532–541, Beth proof language step
findings.source_issue: The proof uses undefined L_1 and L_2 and asserts an equality for the interpolant language, whereas Maehara's lemma supplies an inclusion. After abstracting fresh constants, inclusion in L(Gamma) without R is the needed claim.
findings.minimal_treatment: State the sufficient inclusion and disclose the weakened, defined language bound.

findings.source_locator: interpolation.tex line 545, final Beth proof sentence
findings.source_issue: The conclusion writes !R although the defined predicate symbol throughout the section is R.
findings.minimal_treatment: Use R in the target sentence and disclose the notation correction.

findings.source_locator: interpolation.tex lines 546–551, complete shared theory sufficient condition
findings.source_issue: The source asks only that L(Gamma) be a subset of the common language, but then applies completeness of Gamma to every sentence of the whole common language. A complete theory in a smaller language need not decide such sentences.
findings.minimal_treatment: Require equality with the shared language in this sufficient condition and disclose the strengthened hypothesis.

findings.source_issue: Gamma_1 entailing A does not by itself imply Gamma entailing A. Completeness of Gamma plus consistency of Gamma_1 rules out the alternative Gamma entails not-A; Gamma_2 then entails A, contradicting its assumed entailment of not-A and consistency. The source's final non-entailment is about Gamma instead.
findings.minimal_treatment: Give the correct two-case completeness argument and disclose the reversed step and final-theory repair.

findings.source_issue: Without function symbols, a term may be a variable as well as a constant. Only the constant case creates a new language-symbol concern.
findings.minimal_treatment: Mention the harmless variable case and retain the source's constant case with disclosure.

findings.source_locator: interpolation.tex lines 514–518, Beth proof primed language
findings.source_issue: The section defines L(Gamma') as symbols actually occurring in Gamma'. A theory in L-prime need not use every symbol of the ambient language, so L(Gamma') = L-prime is unwarranted.
findings.minimal_treatment: Define the ambient L-prime without asserting equality to L(Gamma') and disclose the distinction.
